facts.statement: Brachysuchus is an extinct genus of parasuchid phytosaurs named after the Greek words for 'short' and 'Sobek'.
facts.quote: Brachysuchus (from Ancient Greek βραχύς (brakhús), meaning "short", and Σοῦχος (Soûkhos), meaning "Sobek") is an extinct genus of parasuchid phytosaurs

facts.statement: The genus was first named by Case in 1929, with Brachysuchus megalodon designated as the type species.
facts.quote: It was first named by Case in 1929 and the type species is Brachysuchus megalodon.

facts.statement: Fossils of Brachysuchus are found in the Dockum Group in Texas, dating to the Carnian stage of the late Triassic period.
facts.quote: known from the late Triassic period (Carnian stage) of Dockum Group in Texas, United States

facts.statement: Angistorhinus is considered the closest relative of Brachysuchus.
Unlike Angistorhinus, Brachysuchus had a much smaller rostral crest and a shorter, thicker snout.
facts.quote: However, its rostral crest was much smaller than that of Angistorhinus, and the rostrum as a whole is shorter and thicker.

facts.statement: The lower jaws of Brachysuchus expand at the tip into a large bulge that holds its largest tusks.
facts.quote: The lower jaws of Brachysuchus are expanded at the tip to form a large bulge, holding the creature's largest tusks.

facts.statement: There are three tusks on each side of the bulge in the lower jaw.
facts.quote: In the lower jaw, there are three tusks in each side of this protuberance.

facts.statement: Evidence of new tusks forming in sockets indicates that Brachysuchus continuously regrew its teeth throughout its life.
facts.quote: There are new tusks forming in the sockets, indicating that Brachysuchus regrew teeth all its life.

facts.statement: The skull of Brachysuchus is approximately 125 cm long and features a distinctive hooked tip.
facts.quote: The skull is around 125 cm long, with a distinctive hooked tip.

facts.statement: Brachysuchus possessed a comparatively small rostral crest.
facts.quote: It has a comparatively small rostral crest.

facts.statement: Brachysuchus reached a length of approximately eight meters, making it significantly larger than most of its contemporary phytosaur relatives.
facts.quote: Overall Brachysuchus was approximately eight metres long, much bigger than most contemporary phytosaurs.

facts.statement: Brachysuchus likely preyed on heavily armored stegocephalians rather than just fish, utilizing its powerful bite to break through their armor.
facts.quote: Instead of using its jaws to catch fish, it was able to attack and feed off the heavily armoured stegocephalians that roamed the surrounding area

facts.statement: A deformed tip on one lower jaw specimen suggests Brachysuchus used significant force to break through the armor of its prey.
facts.quote: The slightly deformed tip of one specimen's lower jaw suggests that it used a lot of force to break through its prey's armour.

facts.statement: Brachysuchus belongs to the parent group Mystriosuchinae.
Brachysuchus is classified within the family Parasuchidae.
Brachysuchus is classified as a reptile.
Brachysuchus lived between 237 and 205.7 million years ago, spanning the Carnian to Norian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Norian (237 to 205.7 million years ago)

rejected.quote: which show that it had very powerful jaw muscles and a strong bite.
